[1] rewrite

```
- **Why the release check allows runs to differ by 0.5%.** No record says how 0.5%
  was chosen. It dates from an earlier, approximate method, whose runs differed by
  about 0.04% in the alveolar concentration and by more in mixed venous. The same
  check also requires each gap to stay below 1e-14 as a fraction. Any gap that
  breaks 0.5% is at least 1e-8, so it breaks 1e-14 too. Today the 0.5% limit
  changes no outcome.
```

[2] rewrite

```
- **How to change the release check's 0.5% limit.** A fork with an approximate
  method fails 1e-14 even when its arithmetic is correct. A first-order method,
  for example, shows gaps near 1.4e-11. Relax 1e-14, and the 0.5% limit becomes
  the working check. Set that limit above the method's own gaps at these steps and
  below a difference that a learner could see. The constants are in
  `tests/reference/test_sevo_patient.py`.
```

[3] rewrite

```
**The release check on the time step, and why it allows runs to differ by 0.5%.**
The model advances in fixed steps of 0.1 s, and a shorter step should give almost
the same result. Before each release, the check reruns the first minute of the
default sevoflurane induction with steps of 0.1 s, 0.05 s and 0.025 s. Each run's
alveolar, vessel-rich and mixed-venous concentrations must be within 0.5% of the
run with the next shorter step. In a compartment that holds almost no agent, two
values also pass if they differ by less than 0.000001 vol%, because there a tiny
difference is a large percentage. The 0.5% was set for the simulator's earlier
calculation method, at about ten times the 0.04% difference in alveolar
concentration between that method's runs. The current method's runs agree to
better than one part in a trillion (measured 2026-10-03), so the much tighter
limits in the paragraphs above are the ones that would catch a real error.
```

[4] rewrite

```
The 5e-3 relative tolerance was chosen when the simulator used its earlier
calculation method, the operator split. That method showed a relative gap of
4e-4 in the alveolar fraction between steps of 0.1 s and 0.025 s, and 5e-3 is
about ten times that gap. With the current method, the exact step, the same
comparison gives gaps of about 1.4e-13 relative (measured 2026-10-03), so the
tolerance is kept as a coarse check. For a fraction so close to zero that
a relative gap means little, the 1e-8 absolute tolerance lets a negligible
difference pass.
```

[5] rewrite

```
**The release check on the time step, and why it allows runs to differ by 0.5%.**
The simulator moves the model forward in fixed time steps, normally 0.1 s long.
A shorter step should give almost the same result. If it does not, the step is
too long. Before each release, the check runs the first minute of the default
sevoflurane induction three times, with steps of 0.1 s, 0.05 s and 0.025 s. In
each run, the alveolar, vessel-rich and mixed-venous concentrations must be
within 0.5% of the run with the next shorter step. For a compartment that still
holds almost no agent, two values also pass if they differ by less than
0.000001 vol%, which is one part in a hundred million of the gas. There, a tiny
difference can be a large percentage, so a percentage means little. With the
current calculation method, the three runs agree to better than one part in a
trillion (measured 2026-10-03), so this check is now only a coarse safety net.
The much tighter limit in the paragraphs above is the one that would catch a real
error.

The 0.5% margin was set for the simulator's earlier calculation method. With that
method, the alveolar concentrations of the 0.1 s and 0.025 s runs differed by
about 0.04%, so the margin allowed about ten times that difference. The check
compares each run only with the next shorter step. Under the earlier method,
comparing the 0.1 s run directly with the 0.025 s run would have failed, because
their mixed-venous concentrations differed by 0.55%. At one minute, those
concentrations have barely begun to rise.
```

[6] rewrite

```
**The three agents' maximum settings come from two classes of vaporizer.** The sevoflurane and
isoflurane maxima are those of variable-bypass dials. Desflurane's is the top of the Tec 6's range,
and a Tec 6 is a heated gas–vapour blender. The model fixes ambient pressure at 760 mmHg
(§ "Assumptions"). At that pressure, the same dial setting on either class gives the same partial
pressure, so the model does not need to know which class a maximum came from. The classes would
differ only at reduced ambient pressure, which is not modelled (§ "Known limitations").
```
